title: The Thiele Machine: No Free Insight
description:
The Thiele Machine is an abstract model of computation with states, moves, a step, a price per move, and a reading into an ordered set. Its toll requires a positive charge when a move carries the reading somewhere not at or below its previous value. The monograph develops the consequences and examples of that definition, the counting that motivates it, and the argument for choosing it. Permanence and noninterference are additional restrictions where stated. A ledger sums instruction prices; it need not count only raises.

The book studies retained distinctions, merges or fresh states under a total deterministic rule, observation windows, and the room needed to preserve recoverable histories. A two-counter example realizes an earned CHECK, COMMIT and CERTIFY chain. Its universal programs and simulation proofs are supplied in companion Coq files. Physical interpretations require their stated physical premises; the pointer and physical theses are not presented as theorems.

Version 4.1.1 pairs the reviewed 545-page PDF with the matching tagged repository snapshot. The complete 3,728- and 3,735-instruction universal programs reside in that snapshot, not as printed block expansions in the PDF. The publication package consists of both artifacts. The repository includes the monograph source and text, companion proofs, the small-machine implementation, and reproduction instructions. The universal-program companion modules Kernel.UniversalRun and Kernel.PresentedUniversal and their dependencies passed coqchk; this is not a claim that every repository module was rebuilt for this release.
